answer: Each admission burns 40 minutes of single-thread compute on a task bound to the key's hash - the proof is worthless to any other address, so a fleet of 100 fakes pays 4,000 unresellable minutes before casting one vote. Velvet-gloved operators can rent coins or phones, but that gale of rented CPU hours shows up as flat inter-arrival times; an ocean of near-identical latency signatures gets sampled weekly, and each flagged identity forfeits its pending payout. Cost per clone: 40 minutes plus detection risk that grows with fleet size, while one honest vote costs 40 minutes once.
